findings.title: Guard non-table Kimi config values so a bad config skips only Kimi instead of crashing the whole run
findings.body: `kimi_snapshot` assumes the parsed shapes: line 323 calls `(data.get("models") or {}).get(alias)` and line 326 does the same for `providers`, but a TOML-valid config like `default_model = "r"` with `models = "kimi-latest"` (a scalar, e.g. from a user error or a future Kimi config-format drift) passes the subset-equality check at line 318 because `filter_toml` keeps the scalar line and it parses to the identical value; `.get` on a string then raises `AttributeError`. Likewise `default_model = 1` reaches `model_family(1)` and crashes on `(1 or "").lower()` at line 424. `main` only catches `(OSError, ValueError)` around `reviewer_family` (line 629), so the exception escapes, killing the entire run with a traceback and exit code 1 (the documented "findings" code) before codex or claude even attempt, and no result JSON or receipt is written — exactly the "one malformed reviewer config stops every reviewer" failure class this change claims to have fixed.

findings.title: Strip trailing commas in load_jsonc only outside string literals
findings.body: `load_jsonc` handles `//` and `/* */` comments with string-awareness, but then applies `re.sub(r",(\s*[}\]])", r"\1", ...)` to the entire remaining text, including inside string literals. An OpenCode config value that legitimately contains a comma directly before a closing brace or bracket on one line — e.g. `{"provider": {"acme": {"options": {"apiKey": "[REDACTED]"}}}` where the provider's opaque token happens to end in a comma — is silently rewritten to `tok-en}`, so the private OpenCode config carries a corrupted credential or model id and the review fails or runs against the wrong endpoint, with no error surfaced; standard JSONC parsers only strip trailing commas in structural position, so this config loads correctly in the real OpenCode.
